test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 24 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: When an object of mass 'm' falls freely to the ground from a height 'h’, at what point is the object's kinetic energy maximum?

options.text: At one-fourth way through the fall.
At the start of the fall.
When it is about to hit the ground.

solution:
The correct answer is __**When it is about to hit the ground.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When an object falls freely under gravity, its **potential energy is converted to kinetic energy**.
 
• The kinetic energy of an object is given by the formula **KE = 0.5 * m * v²**, where 'm' is mass and 'v' is velocity.
 
• As the object falls, its velocity increases due to acceleration by gravity, leading to **an increase in kinetic energy**.
 
• The **maximum kinetic energy** is achieved **just before the object hits the ground**, as all potential energy has been converted to kinetic energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Potential Energy (PE):**

 
 
• It is the energy possessed by an object due to its position or height above the ground.
 
• PE is calculated using the formula **PE = m * g * h**, where 'm' is mass, 'g' is the acceleration due to gravity, and 'h' is height.
 
 
 
• **Law of Conservation of Energy:**
 
 
• This law states that energy cannot be created or destroyed; it can only be transformed from one form to another.
 
• In the case of a falling object, potential energy is converted to kinetic energy.
 
 
 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity (g):**
 
 
• It is the acceleration experienced by an object due to the gravitational pull of the Earth.
 
• The standard value of 'g' is approximately **9.8 m/s²**.
 
 
 
• **Free Fall:**
 
 
• A condition in which the only force acting on an object is gravity, causing it to fall towards the Earth.
 
• During free fall, air resistance is considered negligible.
